subject.title: Feature Request: Session rotation/archive lifecycle event for cron job triggers

question: Should session archive/rotation automation be supported through core Cron event schedules, through plugin `session_end` plus a narrow SDK/event seam, or should this remain a plugin-owned workflow with no new core surface?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent shape affects public cron configuration, plugin API boundaries, archived-session metadata, and security review; automation should not choose that product boundary alone.

options.title: Use plugin lifecycle plus narrow SDK seam
options.body: Bless `session_end` as the session-boundary signal and add only the smallest safe SDK/event-dispatch capability needed for external plugins to run this workflow.

options.title: Add core cron lifecycle schedules
options.body: Define `schedule.kind: event` for session archive/rotation in cron and Gateway protocol with scoped metadata, persistence, docs, and upgrade/security tests.

options.title: Keep workflow plugin-owned
options.body: Document the current plugin-hook pattern and route self-improving memory automation to a ClawHub/plugin workflow if maintainers decide no new core seam is needed.

recommendation.title: Use plugin lifecycle plus narrow SDK seam
recommendation.body: Bless `session_end` as the session-boundary signal and add only the smallest safe SDK/event-dispatch capability needed for external plugins to run this workflow.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a plugin/API boundary decision, with cron participation after the extension contract is chosen.
